---
title: "Lab 02 — Correlation"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("../R/lab_submission.R")
world <- read_csv("data/country_indicators.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab02", title = "Correlation")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "GDP per capita and life expectancy in this file are…",
  q2 = "What does a positive r tell you?",
  q3 = "Which sentence is acceptable?",
  q4 = "Name one reason a strong correlation might not be a causal effect."
)
```

## What you will do

Read a correlation. Do not turn it into a cause. Then download the `.txt`.

```{r cor-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=3}
cor(world$gdp_per_capita, world$life_expectancy)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Positively correlated (r about 0.75).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Negatively correlated."),
  answer("Uncorrelated (r about 0)."),
  allow_retry = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Above-average X tends to come with above-average Y in these data.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Raising X would raise Y by r units."),
  answer("The p-value is r."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("In these 50 countries, GDP per capita and life expectancy move together (r about 0.75).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The correlation proves that GDP causes longer lives."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "A confounder, reverse causality, or a selected sample.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
